cases.question: Which units are vacant right now?

usage.review_restated: The SQL returns every unit that has no lease whose status is flagged as current, showing its building name, street, unit number, type, bedrooms, square footage and monthly rent, sorted by building name and unit number.

cases.title: Vacant units right now
cases.sql: SELECT b.name AS building_name, b.street AS street, u.unit_number AS unit_number, u.unit_type AS unit_type, u.bedrooms AS bedrooms, u.sqft AS sqft, u.monthly_rent AS monthly_rent FROM unit u JOIN building b ON b.building_id = u.building_id WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM lease l JOIN lease_status s ON s.status_id = l.status_id WHERE l.unit_id = u.unit_id AND s.is_current = 1) ORDER BY b.name, u.unit_number
assumptions: A unit is vacant if it has no lease in a current status (Active - Fixed Term, Active - Month to Month, or Notice Given).
Units whose only leases are Ended, Evicted, or Pending Signature count as vacant, so a unit with a lease still awaiting signature is listed.
Units on Notice Given are treated as still occupied until that lease ends.
Status is taken as stored today (2026-10-21). Current leases have no end dates, and none start in the future.

cases.question: List tenants who currently have a lease, with their unit and monthly rent.

usage.review_restated: This SQL returns one row per lease whose status is flagged as current, showing the tenant's full name, the building name, the unit number, the unit's monthly rent, the status label, and the lease start and end dates, sorted by tenant name.

cases.title: Current tenants with unit and monthly rent
cases.sql: SELECT t.first_name || ' ' || t.last_name AS tenant_name, b.name AS building, u.unit_number AS unit_number, u.monthly_rent AS monthly_rent, ls.label AS lease_status, l.start_date AS lease_start, l.end_date AS lease_end FROM lease l JOIN lease_status ls ON ls.status_id = l.status_id JOIN tenant t ON t.tenant_id = l.tenant_id JOIN unit u ON u.unit_id = l.unit_id JOIN building b ON b.building_id = u.building_id WHERE ls.is_current = 1 ORDER BY tenant_name
assumptions: 'Currently have a lease' means leases whose status is marked as current: Active - Fixed Term, Active - Month to Month, and Notice Given. Ended, Evicted and Pending Signature leases are excluded.
Monthly rent is the rent listed on the unit.
Each current lease is listed on its own line, so a tenant with more than one current lease appears more than once.
Building name is included because unit numbers repeat across buildings.
All buildings and units are covered; no date or other filter was applied.

questions.question: What should count as a maintenance request that is "still open"?
options: All requests not yet closed (open, in progress, waiting for parts)

cases.question: Which tenants paid rent late at least once in 2026?

usage.review_restated: For each tenant who has at least one payment due in 2026 that has a paid date later than its due date, the query returns the tenant's name, email, the count of those late payments, and the latest late paid date, sorted by that count from highest to lowest.

cases.title: Tenants who paid rent late at least once in 2026
cases.sql: SELECT t.tenant_id AS tenant_id, t.first_name || ' ' || t.last_name AS tenant_name, t.email AS email, COUNT(*) AS late_payments_2026, MAX(p.paid_on) AS latest_late_paid_on FROM payment p JOIN lease l ON p.lease_id = l.lease_id JOIN tenant t ON l.tenant_id = t.tenant_id WHERE p.due_on >= '2026-01-01' AND p.due_on < '2027-01-01' AND p.paid_on IS NOT NULL AND p.paid_on <> '' AND p.paid_on > p.due_on GROUP BY t.tenant_id, t.first_name, t.last_name, t.email ORDER BY late_payments_2026 DESC, tenant_name
assumptions: A payment is late when it was paid after its due date, with no grace period.
Only rent due in 2026 (due dates from 2026-01-01 to 2026-10-01) is counted.
Payments with no paid date (44 in 2026) are treated as unpaid, not late, so they are not counted.
Each tenant is listed once, with their number of late payments in 2026 and the date of their most recent late payment.

cases.question: Total rent collected per region in 2026.

usage.review_restated: For each region name, the SQL adds up the amounts of payments whose paid date is non-empty and starts with 2026, using only payments linked through lease, unit and building to a region, and returns the total (rounded to 2 decimals) and the number of payments, sorted by total from highest to lowest.

cases.title: Rent collected per region in 2026
cases.sql: SELECT r.name AS region_name, ROUND(SUM(p.amount),2) AS total_rent_collected, COUNT(*) AS payments_received FROM payment p JOIN lease l ON p.lease_id = l.lease_id JOIN unit u ON l.unit_id = u.unit_id JOIN building b ON u.building_id = b.building_id JOIN region r ON b.region_id = r.region_id WHERE p.paid_on IS NOT NULL AND p.paid_on <> '' AND p.paid_on LIKE '2026-%' GROUP BY r.name ORDER BY total_rent_collected DESC
assumptions: Rent collected means payments that have a recorded paid date, counted by the year the payment was made (calendar 2026).
Payments with no paid date are treated as not collected.
Each payment is assigned to the region of the building that contains the leased unit.
Amounts are summed as recorded; one payment dated after today is included.

Check: The report counts one payment dated after today as collected, but that money has not yet been received, so check that payment and decide whether future-dated payments should be excluded before the totals go to the business user.

cases.question: Urgent maintenance requests that are not closed, with the technician assigned.

usage.review_restated: This returns every maintenance request with priority exactly 'urgent' and a state other than 'closed', across all units and dates, showing its id, unit, category, opened date, state, priority, cost, and the matched staff member's name (or 'Unassigned' when no staff member matches), sorted oldest ope

cases.title: Urgent maintenance requests not closed, with assigned technician
cases.sql: SELECT m.request_id AS request_id, m.unit_id AS unit_id, m.category AS category, m.opened AS opened_date, m.state AS current_state, m.priority AS priority, COALESCE(s.first_name || ' ' || s.last_name, 'Unassigned') AS technician, m.cost AS cost FROM maintenance m LEFT JOIN staff s ON s.staff_id = m.assigned_to AND s.role = 'technician' WHERE m.priority = 'urgent' AND m.state <> 'closed' ORDER BY m.opened
assumptions: 'Urgent' means the request priority is urgent.
'Not closed' means the request status is anything other than closed (open, in progress, or waiting for parts).
The assigned technician is the staff member with the technician role recorded on the request.
Urgent unclosed requests with no technician assigned are still listed, shown as 'Unassigned'.
The list covers all units, buildings and dates, oldest first.

cases.question: Average number of days to close a plumbing request.

usage.review_restated: From the maintenance table, this returns the average of (closed date minus opened date) in days, rounded to one decimal, over rows where category is plumbing, state is closed, and the closed date is present and non-empty, plus a count of those rows (65 here, giving 11.0 days).

cases.title: Average days to close plumbing requests
cases.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(julianday(closed) - julianday(opened)), 1) AS avg_days_to_close, COUNT(*) AS closed_plumbing_requests FROM maintenance WHERE category = 'plumbing' AND state = 'closed' AND closed IS NOT NULL AND closed <> ''
assumptions: A plumbing request is one whose category is plumbing.
Only requests that are closed and have a recorded close date are counted; open, in-progress and waiting-for-parts requests are excluded.
Days to close = close date minus open date, averaged across all such requests.
No date range applied: all plumbing requests of all time are included.
Same-day closures count as 0 days.

cases.question: Leases ending between 2026-10-01 and 2026-12-31.

usage.review_restated: The SQL returns every lease whose end date falls from 1 October 2026 to 31 December 2026 inclusive, showing its lease ID, unit, tenant, status label, start date, end date and deposit, sorted by end date, with no filter on status.

cases.title: Leases ending between 1 Oct and 31 Dec 2026
cases.sql: SELECT l.lease_id AS lease_id, l.unit_id AS unit_id, l.tenant_id AS tenant_id, s.label AS lease_status, l.start_date AS start_date, l.end_date AS end_date, l.deposit AS deposit FROM lease l LEFT JOIN lease_status s ON s.status_id = l.status_id WHERE l.end_date BETWEEN '2026-10-01' AND '2026-12-31' ORDER BY l.end_date
assumptions: Ending means the lease's end date falls from 1 October 2026 to 31 December 2026, inclusive.
All lease statuses are included (both Ended and Evicted leases appear), so no status filter was applied.
Leases with no end date recorded are not included, since they cannot fall in the window.

cases.question: Which buildings have an elevator and more than 10 units?

usage.review_restated: For each building flagged as having an elevator, the query counts its units, keeps only buildings with more than 10 units, and lists them with their name, street, city and unit count, largest first.

cases.title: Buildings with an elevator and more than 10 units
cases.sql: SELECT b.building_id AS building_id, b.name AS building_name, b.street AS street, b.city AS city, COUNT(u.unit_id) AS unit_count FROM building b JOIN unit u ON u.building_id = b.building_id WHERE b.has_elevator = 1 GROUP BY b.building_id, b.name, b.street, b.city HAVING COUNT(u.unit_id) > 10 ORDER BY unit_count DESC
assumptions: 'Has an elevator' means the building is flagged as having an elevator.
'More than 10 units' counts all units in the building, regardless of occupancy or lease status.
No date or location filters were applied.

cases.question: Evicted tenants and their email addresses.

usage.review_restated: This SQL returns one row per lease whose status label is exactly 'Evicted', showing the tenant's full name, the tenant's email, the status label, the lease ID and the lease end date, sorted by last name and first name.

cases.title: Evicted tenants and their email addresses
cases.sql: SELECT t.first_name || ' ' || t.last_name AS tenant_name, t.email AS email, ls.label AS lease_status, l.lease_id AS lease_id, l.end_date AS end_date FROM lease l JOIN tenant t ON t.tenant_id = l.tenant_id JOIN lease_status ls ON ls.status_id = l.status_id WHERE ls.label = 'Evicted' ORDER BY t.last_name, t.first_name
assumptions: 'Evicted tenants' means tenants whose lease has the status Evicted.
One row per evicted lease; a tenant with two evicted leases would appear twice.
No date range applied; all evicted leases are included regardless of end date.
Email is taken from the tenant record.

cases.question: How many plumbin requests are waiting_part?

usage.review_restated: This SQL counts the maintenance requests whose category is plumbing and whose state is waiting_parts, and returns that single count, which is 3.

cases.title: Plumbing requests waiting for parts
cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS waiting_parts_plumbing_requests FROM maintenance WHERE category = 'plumbing' AND state = 'waiting_parts'
assumptions: 'Plumbin' is read as the plumbing category.
'Waiting_part' is read as the 'waiting_parts' status.
All maintenance requests are counted, with no date range or other filter applied.

cases.question: Show open electricle maintenance requests with their unit.

usage.review_restated: Lists electrical maintenance requests whose state is exactly 'open', each with its request date, priority, cost, building name, unit number, unit type, bedrooms and rent, oldest first.

cases.title: Open electrical maintenance requests with unit
cases.sql: SELECT m.request_id AS request_id, m.opened AS opened_date, m.priority AS priority, m.cost AS cost, b.name AS building, u.unit_number AS unit_number, u.unit_type AS unit_type, u.bedrooms AS bedrooms, u.monthly_rent AS monthly_rent FROM maintenance m JOIN unit u ON u.unit_id = m.unit_id JOIN building b ON b.building_id = u.building_id WHERE m.state = 'open' AND m.category = 'electrical' ORDER BY m.opened
assumptions: 'Open' means requests whose status is exactly 'open'; requests that are in progress or waiting for parts are excluded.
'Electrical' (spelled 'electricle' in the request) means the electrical category.
Each request is shown once with its unit number, building name, type, bedrooms and rent.
Oldest requests are listed first.

Check: Confirm that "open" should mean only the exact 'open' state. The report leaves out requests that are in progress or waiting for parts, which many people would still call open, so the list may be incomplete.
